library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Pin the thread count as well as the seed: rxode2 draws random effects in
# parallel, so the simulated cohort otherwise depends on the core count.
rxode2::setRxThreads(1L)

# Model and source

* Citation: Lohmer LRL, Greenwald MK, Kakar R, Laffont CM. Optimal
  buprenorphine exposure to treat patients with opioid use disorder in the era
  of fentanyl and polysubstance use. Front Pharmacol. 2026;17:1839067.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2026.1839067>
* Supplementary Material (model equations):
  <https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fphar.2026.1839067/full#supplementary-material>

Lohmer et al. (2026) pooled two randomised trials of monthly subcutaneous
extended-release buprenorphine (BUP-XR, SUBLOCADE) in adults with moderate to
severe opioid use disorder: the pivotal phase 3 study NCT02357901 ("Study 1",
2015-2016, before fentanyl became prevalent) and NCT04995029 ("Study 2",
2021-2024, a high-risk population in which half the participants used fentanyl
daily). Three exposure-response models were fitted separately in Pumas, so the
paper contributes three model files:

| Model | Endpoint | Structure |
|---|---|---|
| `Lohmer_2026_buprenorphine_opioidUse` | Weekly opioid use (urine screen and self-report both negative = abstinent) | Mixed-effects logistic regression, Emax in buprenorphine concentration; effect compartment in Study 2 |
| `Lohmer_2026_buprenorphine_craving` | Current craving on the 0-100 mm Opioid Craving VAS, categorised 0 / 1-5 / 6-20 / >20 mm | Proportional-odds model, Emax in buprenorphine concentration plus a placebo onset term; effect compartment in Study 2 |
| `Lohmer_2026_buprenorphine_dropout` | Treatment discontinuation | Gompertz hazard with the last observed craving category as a time-varying covariate |

None of the three re-estimates pharmacokinetics. The authors refitted the
Jones 2021 BUP-XR population PK model to both studies and drove the
exposure-response models with the individual predicted plasma
concentrations. That PK model is packaged as `Jones_2021_buprenorphine`, so
this article chains it into the two concentration-driven models, and then
feeds simulated craving into the dropout model, as the authors did when they
used the combined model for evaluation.

```{r load-models}
mod_pk <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jones_2021_buprenorphine"))
mod_use <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lohmer_2026_buprenorphine_opioidUse"))
mod_crav <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lohmer_2026_buprenorphine_craving"))
mod_drop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lohmer_2026_buprenorphine_dropout"))
```

# Population

The efficacy analyses included 989 participants (Table 1): 489 from Study 1
and 500 from Study 2. Study 1 participants were 66.3% male, mean age 39.7
years (SD 11.1), 71.3% White and 26.6% Black/African American; 43.8% reported
injection as their main route of opioid use and 19.8% used
amphetamines/methamphetamines. Study 2 participants were 58.0% male, mean age
41.2 years (SD 10.6), 73.4% White and 20.8% Black/African American; 49.4%
reported daily fentanyl use, 44.0% fentanyl use at least twice a day, 60.0%
amphetamine/methamphetamine use, 29.2% daily fentanyl together with
amphetamines/methamphetamines and 29.2% injection as their main route.
Fentanyl was not assessed in Study 1 and was imputed as absent.

Study 1 randomised participants 2:2:1 to six monthly injections of 300 mg
(300/300 mg), two of 300 mg followed by four of 100 mg (300/100 mg), or
placebo. In Study 2 every participant received 300 mg in Weeks 1 and 2, and at
Week 6 was randomised to eight further monthly injections of 100 mg or 300 mg.
The dropout analysis used 1,071 participants (489 + 582), including Study 2
participants who stopped before the Week 6 randomisation.

The same information is available programmatically through each model's
`population` metadata, e.g.
`readModelDb("Lohmer_2026_buprenorphine_opioidUse")()$population`.

# Source trace

Model equations come from the Supplementary Material ("Opioid Use Model
Equations", "Opioid Craving Model Equations", "Treatment Retention Model
Equations"); parameter values from Tables 2-4. Every `ini()` value carries
the same reference as an in-file comment.

**Opioid use (`Lohmer_2026_buprenorphine_opioidUse`, Table 2)**

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `logite0_study1`, `logite0_study2` | -4.28, -6.83 | Table 2, alpha Study 1 / Study 2 |
| `e_regimen_maint_100mg_logite0` | 0.764 | Table 2, theta alpha 100 mg Study 1 |
| `e_employed_logite0` | 0.796 | Table 2, theta alpha employment |
| `lemax_study1`, `lemax_study2` | log(6.68), log(10.0) | Table 2, Emax Study 1 / Study 2 |
| `e_race_black_emax` | 0.843 | Table 2, theta Emax race |
| `lec50` | log(0.999 ng/mL) | Table 2, EC50 |
| `e_opioid_route_injection_ec50` | 1.74 | Table 2, theta EC50 injection |
| `e_fentanyl_daily_amphetamine_use_ec50` | 8.25 | Table 2, theta EC50 fentanyl/amph |
| `lke0` | log(0.000856 1/h) | Table 2, ke0 Study 2 |
| `etalogite0` | 2.27^2 | Table 2, IIV alpha (SD) |
| `etalec50`, `etalke0` | log(1 + 1.71^2), log(1 + 1.43^2) | Table 2, IIV EC50 171%, ke0 143% |
| logit structure | `alpha + fC + eta` | Supplementary Material |
| Study 2 effect compartment | `d/dt(effect) = ke0 (C - effect)` | Results, "Opioid use model" |

**Opioid craving (`Lohmer_2026_buprenorphine_craving`, Table 3)**

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `logite0_study1`, `logite0_study2` | -5.39, -8.61 | Table 3, alpha1 Study 1 / Study 2 |
| `e_regimen_maint_100mg_logite0` | 0.971 | Table 3, theta alpha 100 mg Study 1 |
| `logitstep1_study1`, `logitstep1_study2` | 2.42, 3.30 | Table 3, delta1 |
| `logitstep2_study1`, `logitstep2_study2` | 1.92, 1.87 | Table 3, delta2 |
| `lemax_study1`, `lemax_study2` | log(2.65), log(3.55) | Table 3, Emax |
| `lec50` | log(0.365 ng/mL) | Table 3, EC50 |
| `e_race_black_emax` | 1.43 | Table 3, theta Emax race |
| `e_fentanyl_ge2_daily_emax` | 0.736 | Table 3, theta Emax fentanyl, no injection |
| `e_fentanyl_ge2_daily_injection_emax` | 0.198 | Table 3, theta Emax fentanyl + injection |
| `emax_placebo` | 3.73 | Table 3, theta Placebo |
| `lke0` | log(0.00217 1/h) | Table 3, ke0 |
| `etalogite0` | 1.71^2 | Table 3, IIV alpha (SD) |
| `etalemax`, `etalec50`, `etalke0` | log(1 + CV^2) for 53.0%, 127%, 190% | Table 3, IIV |
| cumulative logits | `alpha_m + fC + f_placebo + eta` | Supplementary Material |
| placebo term | `theta_placebo (1 - exp(-ke0 t))` | Supplementary Material |

**Dropout (`Lohmer_2026_buprenorphine_dropout`, Table 4)**

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lhaz0_drug`, `lhaz0_placebo` | log(0.00332), log(0.00860) 1/day | Table 4, beta0 BUP-XR / placebo |
| `lkhaz_drug`, `lkhaz_placebo` | log(0.00271), log(0.00906) 1/day | Table 4, ke BUP-XR / placebo |
| `e_opioid_craving_cat2_haz` ... `cat4` | 0.897, 1.04, 2.28 | Table 4, beta1 craving 1-5 / 6-20 / >20 |
| `e_age_haz_drug`, `e_age_haz_placebo` | -0.581, -1.70 | Table 4, beta2 age |
| `e_race_black_haz` | 0.663 | Table 4, beta3 race |
| hazard | `beta0 beta1^craving (AGE/40)^beta2 beta3^RACE exp(-ke t)` | Supplementary Material |

# Virtual cohort

Each study arm gets 150 virtual participants. Baseline characteristics are
drawn to match the per-study frequencies of Table 1. The joint frequencies
that the models use are matched too: in Study 2, 44.0% used fentanyl at least
twice a day (all of them daily users, 49.4%), and only 6.0% combined that with
injection, so injection is drawn conditional on frequent fentanyl use.
Amphetamine/methamphetamine use is drawn independently of daily fentanyl use,
which reproduces the reported 29.2% co-use (0.494 x 0.60 = 0.296). Body weight
and body mass index, which the PK model needs, are not reported by Lohmer
2026 and are drawn around the Jones 2021 cohort (76.5 kg, BMI 24.8 kg/m^2).

```{r cohort}
n_per_arm <- 150

draw_cohort <- function(arm, study2, n, id0) {
  fent_daily <- if (study2 == 1) rbinom(n, 1, 0.494) else rep(0L, n)
  fent_ge2 <- if (study2 == 1) fent_daily * rbinom(n, 1, 0.440 / 0.494) else rep(0L, n)
  inj <- if (study2 == 1) {
    rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(fent_ge2 == 1, 0.060 / 0.440, (0.292 - 0.060) / 0.560))
  } else {
    rbinom(n, 1, 0.438)
  }
  age_mean <- if (study2 == 1) 41.2 else 39.7
  age_sd <- if (study2 == 1) 10.6 else 11.1
  age_rng <- if (study2 == 1) c(18, 72) else c(19, 64)
  data.frame(
    id = id0 + seq_len(n),
    arm = arm,
    STUDY_NCT04995029 = study2,
    REGIMEN_MAINT_100MG = as.integer(arm %in% c("Study 1 300/100 mg", "Study 2 300/100 mg")),
    PLACEBO = as.integer(arm == "Study 1 placebo"),
    EMPLOYED = rbinom(n, 1, if (study2 == 1) 0.394 else 0.337),
    RACE_BLACK = rbinom(n, 1, if (study2 == 1) 0.208 else 0.266),
    AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, age_mean, age_sd), age_rng[1]), age_rng[2]),
    OPIOID_ROUTE_INJECTION = inj,
    FENTANYL_DAILY = fent_daily,
    FENTANYL_GE2_DAILY = fent_ge2,
    AMPHETAMINE_USE = rbinom(n, 1, if (study2 == 1) 0.600 else 0.198),
    WT = exp(rnorm(n, log(76.5), 0.2)),
    BMI = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 24.8, 4), 18), 40)
  )
}

arms <- data.frame(
  arm = c(
    "Study 1 300/300 mg", "Study 1 300/100 mg", "Study 1 placebo",
    "Study 2 300/300 mg", "Study 2 300/100 mg"
  ),
  study2 = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1)
)
cohort <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  draw_cohort(arms$arm[i], arms$study2[i], n_per_arm, (i - 1) * n_per_arm)
}))
cohort |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    `Black/AA (%)` = round(100 * mean(RACE_BLACK)),
    `Injection (%)` = round(100 * mean(OPIOID_ROUTE_INJECTION)),
    `Daily fentanyl + amph (%)` = round(100 * mean(FENTANYL_DAILY * AMPHETAMINE_USE)),
    `Fentanyl >= 2/day + injection (%)` = round(100 * mean(FENTANYL_GE2_DAILY * OPIOID_ROUTE_INJECTION)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

# Buprenorphine exposure (Jones 2021 PK model)

Doses follow the protocols: Study 1 injections every 28 days from Day 1;
Study 2 injections on Day 1 and Day 8, then from Week 6 (Day 36) every 28 days
for eight injections. The transmucosal buprenorphine run-in before the first
injection is not simulated (its concentrations have washed out within days),
so placebo participants have a concentration of zero throughout. A BUP-XR dose
goes into both `depot_fast1` and `depot_slow1`, which the Jones model splits
between its fast and slow pathways.

```{r pk}
dose_times <- function(arm) {
  if (grepl("^Study 1", arm)) {
    (0:5) * 672
  } else {
    c(0, 168, 840 + (0:7) * 672)
  }
}
dose_amts <- function(arm) {
  switch(arm,
    "Study 1 300/300 mg" = rep(300, 6),
    "Study 1 300/100 mg" = c(300, 300, rep(100, 4)),
    "Study 2 300/300 mg" = rep(300, 10),
    "Study 2 300/100 mg" = c(300, 300, rep(100, 8))
  )
}
end_h <- function(study2) ifelse(study2 == 1, 38 * 168, 25 * 168)

active <- cohort |> filter(PLACEBO == 0)
pk_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(active)), function(i) {
  s <- active[i, ]
  tt <- dose_times(s$arm)
  aa <- dose_amts(s$arm)
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = s$id, time = rep(tt, each = 2), amt = rep(aa, each = 2),
    evid = 1, cmt = rep(c("depot_fast1", "depot_slow1"), length(tt))
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = s$id, time = seq(0, end_h(s$STUDY_NCT04995029), by = 24),
    amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central"
  )
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(WT = s$WT, BMI = s$BMI, FORM_BPN_FILM = 1, DOSE_BPN_SL_MG = 0)
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = pk_events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, time, Cc)

conc <- sim_pk |>
  rename(CP_BPN_NGML = Cc) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, arm), by = "id")
conc |>
  filter(time >= 20 * 168) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(`Median Cc weeks 20-25+ (ng/mL)` = signif(median(CP_BPN_NGML), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The 100-mg and 300-mg maintenance doses settle around the 2-3 and 5-6 ng/mL
the paper discusses.

## NCA of the simulated exposure (PKNCA)

The exposure-response models take the concentration as an input, so the
paper reports no NCA. As a check on the exposure that drives them, this is
the NCA of the last dosing interval of the Study 1 arms (Day 141-169).

```{r pknca}
last_int <- conc |>
  filter(grepl("^Study 1", arm), time >= 3360, time <= 4032) |>
  mutate(tad = time - 3360)
dose_last <- last_int |>
  distinct(id, arm) |>
  mutate(tad = 0, dose = ifelse(arm == "Study 1 300/300 mg", 300, 100))
pk_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(last_int, CP_BPN_NGML ~ tad | arm + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_last, dose ~ tad | arm + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 672, cmax = TRUE, cav = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(pk_obj)
summary(nca)
```

# Opioid use

`CP_BPN_NGML` is supplied on every daily record; `covsInterpolation =
"linear"` lets the Study 2 effect compartment integrate a smooth input. The
cohort mean of the individual probabilities of abstinence (with
between-subject variability) is compared with the observed proportions of
Figure 1.

```{r pd-data}
pd_grid <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohort)), function(i) {
  s <- cohort[i, ]
  data.frame(id = s$id, time = seq(0, end_h(s$STUDY_NCT04995029), by = 24))
})) |>
  left_join(conc |> select(id, time, CP_BPN_NGML), by = c("id", "time")) |>
  mutate(CP_BPN_NGML = ifelse(is.na(CP_BPN_NGML), 0, CP_BPN_NGML), evid = 0) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id")
```

```{r opioid-use}
sim_use <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_use,
  events = pd_grid,
  keep = "arm",
  covsInterpolation = "linear",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
use_week <- sim_use |>
  filter(time %% 168 == 0, time > 0) |>
  mutate(week = time / 168) |>
  group_by(arm, week) |>
  summarise(pct_abstinent = 100 * mean(prob_opioid_abstinence), .groups = "drop")
```

Observed percentages read from Figure 1 by the maintainers:

```{r fig1-digitised}
fig1 <- tribble(
  ~arm, ~week, ~observed,
  "Study 1 300/100 mg", 5, 57,
  "Study 1 300/100 mg", 13, 56,
  "Study 1 300/100 mg", 25, 63,
  "Study 1 300/300 mg", 5, 48,
  "Study 1 300/300 mg", 13, 55,
  "Study 1 300/300 mg", 25, 66,
  "Study 1 placebo", 5, 20,
  "Study 1 placebo", 13, 11,
  "Study 1 placebo", 25, 6,
  "Study 2 300/300 mg", 2, 24,
  "Study 2 300/300 mg", 6, 30,
  "Study 2 300/300 mg", 10, 38,
  "Study 2 300/300 mg", 22, 43,
  "Study 2 300/300 mg", 38, 51,
  "Study 2 300/100 mg", 2, 18,
  "Study 2 300/100 mg", 6, 31,
  "Study 2 300/100 mg", 10, 37,
  "Study 2 300/100 mg", 22, 45,
  "Study 2 300/100 mg", 38, 48
)
cmp_use <- fig1 |>
  left_join(use_week, by = c("arm", "week")) |>
  mutate(simulated = round(pct_abstinent, 1), diff = round(simulated - observed, 1))
cmp_use |>
  select(arm, week, observed, simulated, diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Arm = arm, Week = week, `Observed (%)` = observed,
    `Simulated (%)` = simulated, `Difference (points)` = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1 of Lohmer 2026: percentage of participants abstinent by week and arm. Lines: cohort mean of the simulated individual probabilities; points: observed values read from Figure 1."}
ggplot(use_week, aes(week, pct_abstinent, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig1, aes(week, observed, colour = arm), size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ ifelse(grepl("^Study 1", arm), "Study 1", "Study 2"), scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Study week", y = "Participants abstinent (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r check-use}
stopifnot(
  # A transcription error in an intercept or Emax moves a whole arm by tens
  # of points; the median gap across all digitised points stays small.
  abs(median(cmp_use$diff)) < 6,
  quantile(abs(cmp_use$diff), 0.9) < 15
)
```

## Effect of daily fentanyl plus amphetamine co-use (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows that in Study 2 the participants who used both daily fentanyl
and amphetamines/methamphetamines were the least abstinent on the 100-mg
maintenance dose, and caught up with the others on 300 mg. The model carries
this through an 8.25-fold higher EC50.

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates the pattern of Figure 3 of Lohmer 2026: simulated abstinence in Study 2 by maintenance dose and daily fentanyl plus amphetamine/methamphetamine co-use."}
fig3 <- sim_use |>
  filter(time %% 168 == 0, time > 0, grepl("^Study 2", arm)) |>
  mutate(
    week = time / 168,
    group = ifelse(FENTANYL_DAILY * AMPHETAMINE_USE == 1,
      "Daily fentanyl + amphetamine", "Other"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(arm, group, week) |>
  summarise(pct = 100 * mean(prob_opioid_abstinence), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(fig3, aes(week, pct, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(x = "Study week", y = "Participants abstinent (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig3-gap}
gap <- fig3 |>
  filter(week >= 30) |>
  group_by(arm, group) |>
  summarise(pct = mean(pct), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = pct) |>
  mutate(gap = Other - `Daily fentanyl + amphetamine`)
knitr::kable(gap, digits = 1)
```

The subgroup has only a few dozen simulated participants per arm, so the
check is made on the typical participant instead: Study 2 at Week 38 with a
constant concentration equal to the simulated median of each maintenance
dose. The comparison is on the logit scale, where the drug effect acts: the
8.25-fold EC50 leaves the co-use participant on the rising part of the Emax
curve at 100-mg concentrations, so 300 mg adds more to the logit. (On the
probability scale the typical "other" participant, with a random effect of
zero, sits on the steep middle of the logistic curve, which hides this.)

```{r typical-helper}
typical_grid <- function(cp, covs) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(cp), function(i) {
    data.frame(id = i, time = seq(0, 38 * 168, by = 24), CP_BPN_NGML = cp[i], evid = 0) |>
      bind_cols(covs[i, , drop = FALSE])
  }))
}
base_covs <- data.frame(
  STUDY_NCT04995029 = 1, REGIMEN_MAINT_100MG = 0, EMPLOYED = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0,
  OPIOID_ROUTE_INJECTION = 0, FENTANYL_DAILY = 0, FENTANYL_GE2_DAILY = 0,
  AMPHETAMINE_USE = 0
)
```

```{r check-fig3}
cp_ss <- c(2.66, 6.88, 2.66, 6.88)
covs3 <- base_covs[rep(1, 4), ]
covs3$FENTANYL_DAILY <- c(0, 0, 1, 1)
covs3$AMPHETAMINE_USE <- c(0, 0, 1, 1)
typ3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_use, "omega"), events = typical_grid(cp_ss, covs3), returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(time == 38 * 168) |>
  mutate(
    dose = rep(c("100 mg", "300 mg"), 2),
    group = rep(c("Other", "Daily fentanyl + amphetamine"), each = 2)
  ) |>
  select(group, dose, logit_opioid_abstinence, prob_opioid_abstinence)
knitr::kable(typ3, digits = 3)
p3 <- function(g, d) typ3$logit_opioid_abstinence[typ3$group == g & typ3$dose == d]
# The co-use subgroup gains more from 300 mg than the other participants do.
stopifnot(
  p3("Daily fentanyl + amphetamine", "300 mg") - p3("Daily fentanyl + amphetamine", "100 mg") >
    p3("Other", "300 mg") - p3("Other", "100 mg")
)
```

# Opioid craving

```{r craving}
sim_crav <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_crav,
  events = pd_grid,
  keep = "arm",
  covsInterpolation = "linear",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
crav_gt20 <- sim_crav |>
  filter(time %% 168 == 0, time > 0) |>
  mutate(study = ifelse(grepl("^Study 1", arm), "Study 1", "Study 2")) |>
  group_by(study) |>
  summarise(pct_gt20 = 100 * mean(prob_opioid_craving_gt20), .groups = "drop")
crav_gt20 |>
  mutate(published = c(6, 20)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Study = study, `Simulated craving > 20 mm (%)` = pct_gt20,
    `Published (%)` = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

The Discussion reports clinically significant craving (>20 mm) in 20% of
Study 2 and 6% of Study 1 participants. The simulated weekly averages are in
the same range and keep the order between studies. The Study 1 figure here
includes the placebo arm, whose craving is higher.

```{r check-craving}
stopifnot(
  crav_gt20$pct_gt20[crav_gt20$study == "Study 2"] >
    crav_gt20$pct_gt20[crav_gt20$study == "Study 1"] - 5,
  abs(crav_gt20$pct_gt20[crav_gt20$study == "Study 2"] - 20) < 12
)
```

```{r fig4, fig.cap = "Pattern of Figure 4 of Lohmer 2026: simulated probability of craving > 20 mm in Study 2 by frequent fentanyl use (>= 2 times/day) and injection as the main route."}
fig4 <- sim_crav |>
  filter(time %% 168 == 0, time > 0, grepl("^Study 2", arm)) |>
  mutate(
    week = time / 168,
    group = case_when(
      FENTANYL_GE2_DAILY == 1 & OPIOID_ROUTE_INJECTION == 1 ~ "Fentanyl >= 2/day + injection",
      FENTANYL_GE2_DAILY == 1 ~ "Fentanyl >= 2/day, no injection",
      OPIOID_ROUTE_INJECTION == 1 ~ "Injection, no frequent fentanyl",
      TRUE ~ "Neither"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(group, week) |>
  summarise(pct_gt20 = 100 * mean(prob_opioid_craving_gt20), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(fig4, aes(week, pct_gt20, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Study week", y = "Craving > 20 mm (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

As in Figure 4, frequent fentanyl users who inject have the highest
craving. Only about 6% of Study 2 participants are in that group, so the
ordering is checked on the typical participant (Week 38, 300-mg median
concentration).

```{r check-fig4}
covs4 <- base_covs[rep(1, 4), ]
covs4$FENTANYL_DAILY <- c(0, 1, 0, 1)
covs4$FENTANYL_GE2_DAILY <- c(0, 1, 0, 1)
covs4$OPIOID_ROUTE_INJECTION <- c(0, 0, 1, 1)
typ4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_crav, "omega"), events = typical_grid(rep(6.88, 4), covs4), returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(time == 38 * 168) |>
  mutate(group = c("Neither", "Fentanyl >= 2/day, no injection", "Injection, no frequent fentanyl", "Fentanyl >= 2/day + injection")) |>
  select(group, prob_opioid_craving_gt20)
knitr::kable(typ4, digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  typ4$prob_opioid_craving_gt20[4] == max(typ4$prob_opioid_craving_gt20),
  # No main effect of injection on craving was retained.
  abs(typ4$prob_opioid_craving_gt20[3] - typ4$prob_opioid_craving_gt20[1]) < 1e-8
)
```

# Treatment retention

To drive the dropout model, a craving category is drawn for every
participant at each protocol visit from the simulated category probabilities
(weekly in Study 1; weekly to Week 10 and then every 4 weeks to Week 38 in
Study 2), and carried forward day by day. Time in the dropout model is in
days.

```{r dropout}
visit_weeks <- function(study2) {
  if (study2 == 1) c(0:10, seq(14, 38, by = 4)) else 0:25
}
visits <- sim_crav |>
  select(id, time, starts_with("prob_opioid_craving_le")) |>
  mutate(week = time / 168) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, STUDY_NCT04995029), by = "id") |>
  group_by(id) |>
  filter(week %in% visit_weeks(first(STUDY_NCT04995029))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    u = runif(n()),
    cat = 1 + (u > prob_opioid_craving_le0) + (u > prob_opioid_craving_le5) +
      (u > prob_opioid_craving_le20),
    day = week * 7
  ) |>
  select(id, day, cat)

drop_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohort)), function(i) {
  s <- cohort[i, ]
  data.frame(id = s$id, time = seq(0, end_h(s$STUDY_NCT04995029) / 24, by = 1))
})) |>
  left_join(visits, by = c("id", "time" = "day")) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  tidyr::fill(cat, .direction = "down") |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(OPIOID_CRAVING_CAT = cat, evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz") |>
  select(-cat) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, arm, AGE, RACE_BLACK, PLACEBO), by = "id")

sim_drop <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_drop, events = drop_events, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
surv <- sim_drop |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(survival = mean(sur), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(panel = case_when(
    arm == "Study 1 placebo" ~ "Study 1 placebo",
    grepl("^Study 1", arm) ~ "Study 1 BUP-XR",
    TRUE ~ "Study 2 BUP-XR"
  )) |>
  group_by(panel, time) |>
  summarise(survival = mean(survival), .groups = "drop")
```

Survival read from the observed Kaplan-Meier lines of Figure 5 by the
maintainers:

```{r fig5-digitised}
fig5 <- tribble(
  ~panel, ~time, ~observed,
  "Study 1 BUP-XR", 50, 0.87,
  "Study 1 BUP-XR", 100, 0.76,
  "Study 1 BUP-XR", 150, 0.69,
  "Study 1 placebo", 50, 0.58,
  "Study 1 placebo", 100, 0.45,
  "Study 1 placebo", 150, 0.38,
  "Study 2 BUP-XR", 50, 0.78,
  "Study 2 BUP-XR", 100, 0.66,
  "Study 2 BUP-XR", 200, 0.54,
  "Study 2 BUP-XR", 250, 0.49
)
cmp_drop <- fig5 |>
  left_join(surv, by = c("panel", "time")) |>
  mutate(simulated = round(survival, 3), diff = round(simulated - observed, 3))
cmp_drop |>
  select(panel, time, observed, simulated, diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Panel = panel, `Day` = time, `Observed survival` = observed,
    `Simulated survival` = simulated, Difference = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r fig5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Lohmer 2026: treatment retention. Lines: mean simulated survival; points: observed Kaplan-Meier values read from Figure 5."}
ggplot(surv, aes(time, survival)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = fig5, aes(time, observed)) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Survival") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r check-dropout}
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cmp_drop$diff)) < 0.06,
  quantile(abs(cmp_drop$diff), 0.9) < 0.12
)
```

The typical-value hazards alone show the size of the craving effect: a
participant with craving above 20 mm throughout has about twice the hazard.

```{r dropout-typical}
typ <- expand.grid(time = c(0, 50, 100, 150, 200), OPIOID_CRAVING_CAT = 1:4) |>
  mutate(id = OPIOID_CRAVING_CAT, AGE = 40, RACE_BLACK = 0, PLACEBO = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz") |>
  arrange(id, time)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_drop, events = typ, returnType = "data.frame")
sim_typ |>
  filter(time == 200) |>
  transmute(`Craving category` = c("0 mm", "1-5 mm", "6-20 mm", "> 20 mm")[id], `Survival at Day 200` = round(sur, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Craving model, which study has the effect compartment.** Table 3 labels
  ke0 "Equilibrium rate constant for response in study 1 and placebo effect",
  but the Results ("the same equilibration rate ke0 ... described the time to
  maximal placebo effect in Study 1 and the slower treatment response in
  Study 2") and the Discussion ("the model for opioid craving incorporated an
  effect compartment for Study 2") place the effect compartment in Study 2.
  The maintainers follow the Results and Discussion and read "study 1" in the
  Table 3 label as a slip.
* **Craving model, placebo term in every participant.** The printed final
  equation adds `f_placebo = theta_placebo (1 - exp(-ke0 t))` to every
  cumulative logit with no study or arm restriction, and the model applies it
  so. Restricting it to Study 1 would put about half of Study 2 above 20 mm
  late in treatment, against the low mean craving of Figure 4; restricting it
  to the placebo arm would make placebo participants crave less than treated
  ones.
* **Log-normal variability.** Tables 2 and 3 report CV%; the variances use
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`, the convention of the same group's Jones 2021
  PK model, whose Table 3 prints true CVs (variance 0.704 = 101% CV). The
  intercept variability is additive and reported as an SD, so its variance is
  the square of the SD.
* **Covariate effects as multiplicative factors.** The "coefficient on"
  parameters of Tables 2-4 are applied as multipliers (`theta^X` for an
  indicator `X`). The Results prose confirms the direction and size of each
  (1.74x and 8.25x EC50, Emax 16% lower, 43% higher, 26% and 80% lower;
  dropout 34% lower; craving > 20 mm doubles the hazard). The intercepts are
  negative, so the employment factor 0.796 raises the drug-free probability
  of abstinence, as the Results state.
* **Composite covariates are formed in the model.** The paper's composites
  ("daily fentanyl and amphetamine/methamphetamine co-use", "fentanyl >= 2
  times/day and injection use") are products of separate indicators
  (`FENTANYL_DAILY * AMPHETAMINE_USE`, `FENTANYL_GE2_DAILY *
  OPIOID_ROUTE_INJECTION`). "Fentanyl >= 2 times/day with no injection" and
  "with injection" are mutually exclusive factors (0.736 and 0.198), not
  cumulative.
* **The Study 1 100-mg arm effect** applies from randomisation (Day 1), in
  Study 1 only, as "100-mg arm effect in Study 1" states; the models multiply
  `REGIMEN_MAINT_100MG` by `1 - STUDY_NCT04995029`.
* **Time origin.** Time zero is the first BUP-XR or placebo injection, both
  for the effect compartments and for the placebo and Gompertz terms. The
  opioid use and craving models run in hours (ke0 in 1/h, as printed); the
  dropout model runs in days (beta0 and ke in 1/day).
* **Effect compartment initial state.** The effect compartment starts at
  zero at the first injection, ignoring any transmucosal buprenorphine given
  before it; the paper does not state its initial condition.
* **Exposure for this article.** The authors used individual predictions from
  the Jones 2021 model refitted to both studies (empirical Bayes estimates
  that are not published). Here the published Jones 2021 typical values and
  variability drive the simulation, without the transmucosal run-in. Body
  weight and BMI are not reported by Lohmer 2026 and were drawn around the
  Jones 2021 cohort.
* **Comparison targets.** Figures 1 and 5 are observed data. The observed
  proportions in Figure 1 come from participants still in the study, while
  the simulation averages over the full cohort and ignores dropout; under
  the missing-at-random dropout the authors found, this mainly affects late
  weeks. The craving percentages are the Discussion's study-level figures.
* **Values read from figures.** The observed points of Figures 1 and 5 were
  read from the published figures by the maintainers and carry reading error
  of a few percentage points.
```
